**NTRT pre-market gap brief — 2026-11-03 (Tue)**

- **Mode B —
- screener fallback.** `NTRT_BASE_URL` was unset and `GET http://127.0.0.1:8000/health` returned no response (HTTP 000) at 09:08 ET, so the backend was unavailable and the brief was built from the TradingView public screener —
- the only source in this runtime that returns **pre-market volume** alongside the pre-market print.
- Prior close for every name was independently re-verified against Yahoo daily bars (Nov 2 regular close) — 13/13 exact matches.

Snapshot: **09:07 ET**, 25 minutes before the open. This is a live pre-market tape and it was still moving when the scan was taken.

**TL;DR**

- **261 names gapped ≥3%** (210 up, 51 down) — a wide tape, but the *quality* of it is poor:
**159 of 261 names traded under 1% of their 30-day average daily volume**, so the median gap in this screen is a quote, not a market.

- **The only names worth trading are the 25 with ≥5% of ADV.** Among those the real story is
- earnings dispersion, not a macro move:
- **SHOP -15.6% on 12.6% of ADV** is the single most consequential print in the screen (a $201B market cap) and it is a *GMV-miss*, not a profit miss.

- **Today's tape is one-directional and event-driven.** Election day plus a heavy post-earnings
season. Futures were mixed (Dow -0.5%, S&P flat, Nasdaq +0.4%) — so every big move below is idiosyncratic, not beta.

**Catalysts**

- **The dominant theme is guidance quality, not earnings.** Nine of the twelve deep-dive names missed or met on the top line but were sold or bought on the **forward** number —
- the guidance midpoint, the contract-value line, or the margin. AAPL, PLTR, ZBRA, DT and SHOP all beat or met revenue and were still crushed.
- That is the tape's shape today, and it is worth carrying into the open.

- **SHOP (-15.6%)** — the most consequential single print. Revenue and EPS were fine; **GMV missed
- and decelerated from 31.6% to 29.5% y/y**. Because merchant revenue is a take-rate on GMV, the market is pricing a slower top line into 2027.
- FY26 guide of only "low-30s%" revenue growth did not help.

- **PLTR (-5.9%)** — Q3 revenue +96% to $2.31B and an EPS beat, and both FY26 operating-profit and
FCF guidance were *raised*. The sell-off is entirely on **total contract value growth decelerating to +6% from +49%** (US commercial +11%). This is a bookings-slowdown story, not a demand story.

- **AAPL (-4.3%)** — Q4 profit beat; the gross-margin outlook disappointed. ~$190B of market cap
gone pre-open.

- **DT (-15.1%)** — revenue and ARR both beat and the ARR/revenue guidance was *raised*, but FY27
adj EPS was cut to $1.88–1.90 against a $1.98 consensus and FCF to $600–605M from $610–615M.

- **ZBRA (-14.7%)** — beat on both lines, then guided Q4 EPS to a $5.20 midpoint vs $5.21 consensus
and posted a 230bp gross-margin decline on memory-component costs.

- **BLZE (+33.4%)** — the cleanest fundamental story in the screen: revenue +26%, B2 +47%, margin
expansion, guidance raised, and contracted NeoCloud demand loading earlier than expected.

- **LSCC (+13.2%)** — record revenue $291M (+118% y/y) against a $256M consensus, adj EPS $0.72 vs
$0.55, Q4 guide ~14% above consensus, ≥60% FY27 growth guided, backlog into 1H 2028, and a wave of price-target raises.

- **GRAB (+10.5%)** — beat-and-raise on both revenue and adj EBITDA, with Financial Services turning
profitable for the first time and $400M of buybacks executed.

- **FISV (+9.7%)** — adj EPS $1.75 beat and adjusted revenue $4.85B beat; FY26 organic revenue and
adj EPS outlook affirmed; Project Elevate savings target doubled to $1B. The headline GAAP loss of $11.17/sh is a $6.45B **non-cash goodwill impairment**, and the stock rallied anyway.

- **ADEA (-19.9%)** / **EBS (-19.7%)** — the two cleanest guidance cuts of the day. ADEA cut FY26
revenue to $375–415M on delayed media license deals; EBS cut for a second straight year and announced its CFO's retirement.

- **DOCN** — worth noting as the counter-example: a strong Q3 (rev $321M +40%, record $160M ARR
- added, outlook raised) that was *sold anyway*. The market is paying for execution and punishing anything that looks like a good-but-not-good-enough print.
- **It dropped out of the ≥3% screen between scans** — the gap faded from -3.1% to -2.5% by 09:08 —
- but on 881K shares it was still the heaviest pre-market volume in the whole screen (34% of ADV), so the selling was real even though the gap closed.

- **BRCC (-16.3%)** — revenue in line, GAAP loss far worse than consensus on Outpost impairments and
a legal accrual, FY26 guidance merely held after a +34% one-month run.

- **BVS (-13.8%)** — adj EPS beat, but FY26 revenue cut ~$12M at the midpoint on bone-graft
substitutes; a strategic review is running without a timeline.

**Needs human eyes**

- **BRAI +19.2% on 32.4% of ADV** — the heaviest pre-market book in the screen, and the only
- top-20 name where I could **not** confirm a hard catalyst. Chartmill shows a 13.8% after-hours gain on Nov 2 with no clear news attached;
- Benzinga headlines a "jumps 56% after hours" story that does not line up with the price action. Treat as momentum until a filing or press release surfaces.

- **Thin-book prints** — CWH (-10.7%, 0.1% of ADV), ACIC (-8.3%, 350 shares), DRUG (-7.8%, 344
shares), AEIS (+12.5%, 0.7%), DRVN (-10.9%, 0.9%), STVN (-13.9%, 0.9%). These are quotes, not markets. They are excluded from the actionable set above for that reason.

- **STVN (-13.9%)** — Q3 was reported pre-open, but the consensus I can source is ~$0.17–0.18 EPS
- on ~$364M revenue with the divestiture already known. I could not find the actual result or a negative catalyst; the gap may be an unexplained print.
- Needs a look at the release.

- **KMDA (-4.2%) and MDGL (+3.2%)** post 13–24% "of ADV" on 20–40K shares. Arithmetic, not
demand.

- **The tape is live.** Snapshot 09:07 ET, open 09:30. Every number here is a pre-open print that
moved several times between 08:00 and 09:07 (BLZE ranged +33.4 to +34.4; SHOP -15.2 to -15.6; DT -15.1 to -15.2). Re-pull before the open if you are trading these.

- **Election day.** Futures were mixed (Dow -0.5%, S&P -0.05%, Nasdaq +0.4%) with the Dow
defensively lower into the vote and October nonfarm payrolls due Friday. Macro risk can land on top of an already busy earnings tape.

**Method & caveats**

- **Primary source:** TradingView public scanner, `POST https://scanner.tradingview.com/america/scan`,
- run **twice** — `premarket_change` in `[3,1000]` (desc) and `[-1000,-3]` (asc) — then merged and ranked by **absolute** `premarket_change`, so both the gain and the decline side are carried.
- 210 gainers + 51 decliners = **261 names**.

- **Filters held exactly as specified:** `type = stock` (**REITs included — do not re-filter**),
`exchange != OTC`, `market_cap_basic >= 200,000,000`, gap ≥ 3%.

- **Importance measure:** `premarket_volume ÷ average_volume_30d_calc` = % of 30-day ADV. This is
the only column that separates a market from a quote, and it is why the two tables above differ from a naive gap ranking.

- **Prior-close verification:** every prior close used for the gap was re-checked against Yahoo
daily bars for Nov 2 — BLZE, SHOP, ADEA, BRAI, AEHR, DT, ZBRA, GRAB, LSCC, FISV, EBS, PLTR and AAPL all matched to the cent. The gap base is sound.

- **Yahoo pre-market prices and ranges were deliberately NOT published.** Yahoo's pre-market tape
- goes stale on thin names and returns volume 0 on every pre-market bar, so it cannot source this brief's importance column at all.
- Where Yahoo was used, it was only for the *prior regular close*, which is a settled regular-session number.

- **Lag:** TradingView pre-market columns are live as of the scan; the screener holds only the
most recent session, so this brief cannot be rebuilt for an older date from this source.

- **Catalyst sourcing:** each "why" was sourced from the issuer's own release/IR page or a
wire/major outlet, never from memory. Where I could not confirm a catalyst, the row says so.

- **Not used:** the ntrt backend (`NTRT_BASE_URL` unset; `GET /health` on the default
`http://127.0.0.1:8000` returned HTTP 000), the `mcp__*` finance tools (not registered here — 0 finance tools in the catalog), and Finviz/Yahoo HTML scraping.
